result:
If I could change one thing about the world, it would be to make sure every child grows up feeling safe, loved, and curious about life.

So much of what we struggle with later—fear, resentment, the need to control, the inability to trust—traces back to those early years. Not always, of course. But often enough.

If every child had at least one person who really saw them, who made them feel like they mattered, I think the ripples would be enormous. Less cruelty. More empathy. People who believe they're worth something tend not to want to tear the world down.

It's not a policy. It's not a grand gesture. It's quiet, and it happens in millions of small rooms, in millions of small moments. But I think it might matter more than almost anything else.

What's yours?
